text.p: Peru's second largest brewery, Compania Cervecera del Sur,, said it is more likely to issue American Despositary Receipts (ADRs) or bonds than take on a new partner during its current higher-than-expected growth cycle.
The company, a Lima blue-chip, was recently widely rumored to be on the brink of a merger.
But "I was the first to be surprised by that rumor," general manager Andres Von Wedemeyer told Reuters in an interview. "We are not looking for a strategic partner."
Cervesur, with its Arequipena and Cuzquena beer brands, entered the Lima market in 1995 to do battle with its traditional rivals, Cerveceria Backus y Johnston and Compania Nacional de Cerveza (CNC).
Backus and CNC, Peru's first and third largest breweries respectively, are due to unite forces in a merger that will take effect from December 30. Both are members of the large Backus Corp.

"We are competing with Peru's biggest industrial conglomerate, but that is how we have grown ... We are the little company seeking and conquering markets," said Von Wedemeyer. "This forces us to make an effort in quality, not only in products but also in services. The breweries are like the cement companies. They grow in large steps."
Cervesur is considering a $40 million expansion of its brewery in the southern city of Arequipa, he added.
The company also aims to take its Cuzquena "Premimum" brand to international markets.
"That is one of our visions for the future. I know it is ambitious but we want to enter the quality international market," said Von Wedemeyer.
The company currently accounts for more than 70 percent of Peruvian beer exports, mainly to the United States, Britain, France, Japan and Chile.
